correctness.rationale: The exact distance-two adjacencies follow from affine incidence axioms and bipartite parity. Every scale-two simplex belongs to the union of two explicitly defined conical shores with intersection the connected graph G_s. Both shores are simply connected; their homotopy-pushout split gives the stated all-order integral wedges. Natural Mayer–Vietoris identifies H2 inclusion with a primitive graph-cycle sublattice; higher homology is an augmentation-lattice tensor; the exceptional q=3 endpoint kernel is exactly the two new shore summands. Standalone finite independent face/boundary and inclusion computations for q=3 confirm ranks and stage maps; q=4 checks metric structure. Finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Line faults within a genuine affine parallel class are a canonical geometric degradation, not an arbitrary hand-picked slice. Intermediate topology and exact integral inclusion maps quantify linear primitive cycle-class loss and exponential high-sphere-class loss, with a nontrivial dimension shift and exceptional new kernel at complete erasure. The two known endpoint homotopy types alone do not determine these intervening invariants or stability maps. The classification holds for all existing affine-plane orders >=3 without coordinatization, providing an exact structural threshold and a natural test family for topology under metric recomputation.
